topics.label: Introduction to Complement
topics.groupedBecause: It opens the lecture by framing the importance and complexity of the complement system in immunology.

topics.label: Foundational Concepts, Nomenclature, and C3 Function
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the overarching architecture, naming rules, and central molecular role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the mechanisms through which the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways trigger complement activation.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the primary downstream immunological processes by which activated complement clears pathogens.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It analyzes the distinct disease manifestations and diagnostic presentations associated with deficiencies in complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how microbial pathogens have evolved strategies to counteract and survive complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Conclusion and Upcoming Topics
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing framing for the session and introduces the subject of the next lecture.
